schedule.title: Weekend Itinerary
schedule.subtitle: Three memorable days in the shadow of the Bucegi Mountains

events.title: Peleș Castle Royal Tour & Sinaia Gardens
events.description: Exclusive timed group tour of King Carol I's Neo-Renaissance masterpiece, featuring German woodwork, 160 royal chambers, and magnificent landscaped terraces. Private group entry passes provided for all wedding guests.

events.title: Carpathian Welcome Gathering & Toasts
events.description: An informal mountain gathering featuring traditional Romanian delicacies, local artisanal cheeses, Romanian wines, and a traditional țuică and pălincă welcome toast.

events.title: Guest Arrival & Welcome Refreshments
events.description: Guests arrive at the historic castle gates. Sparkling wine, mountain berry elixirs, and views of the Caraiman Massif.

events.title: Garden Nuptial Ceremony
events.description: Vows exchanged overlooking the towering cliffs of the Bucegi Mountains and the Caraiman Cross.

events.title: Cocktail Hour & Castle Exploration
events.description: Acoustic violin and cello, canapés, wine tasting, and guided viewings of the castle's stained-glass windows and historic masonry.

events.title: The Royal Banquet & Midnight Dancing
events.description: Multi-course feast blending contemporary European fine dining with rich Romanian culinary heritage. Live band, dancing, and midnight revelry beneath the illuminated Caraiman Peak.

events.title: Farewell Recovery Brunch
events.description: Fresh mountain espresso, local pastries (plăcinte & cozonac), fresh berries, and light bites to reminisce about the night before.

events.title: High Alpine Cable Car or Bran Castle Excursion
events.location: Bucegi Plateau (Babele & Sphinx) or Bran Castle
events.description: Choose your adventure: Take the Telecabina Bușteni cable car 2,200 meters up to the ancient rock formations of Babele and the enigmatic Romanian Sphinx, or take an organized day excursion to legendary Bran Castle ('Dracula's Castle').

travel.title: Travel & Journey
travel.subtitle: Navigating from North America to the heart of Romania
travel.flightsLead: Most guests will depart from San Diego (SAN) or Los Angeles (LAX) heading into Bucharest Henri Coandă International Airport (OTP) or Brașov-Ghimbav International (GHV).

sanOpt.detail: SAN -> MUC -> OTP. Extremely reliable connections, modern aircraft, seamless luggage transit, and consistent arrival times into Bucharest in the early afternoon.

baOpt.detail: SAN -> LHR -> OTP. Convenient daytime departure from San Diego, smooth transatlantic leg, and frequent daily flights from Heathrow to OTP.

klmOpt.airline: KLM / Air France via Amsterdam (AMS) or Paris (CDG)
klmOpt.detail: SAN -> AMS/CDG -> OTP. High daily frequency and pleasant European transfer hubs.

laxOpt.airline: Turkish Airlines via Istanbul (IST) or Star Alliance from LAX
laxOpt.detail: For guests departing from Los Angeles (LAX), Turkish Airlines via IST offers award-winning service and direct connections into OTP.

memorialDayWarning.title: Memorial Day Weekend Flight Advisory
memorialDayWarning.text: Memorial Day in the United States falls on Monday, May 31, 2027. Because transatlantic return flights around Memorial Day experience elevated demand, we strongly urge all guests to book airline tickets 6 to 9 months ahead (between August and November 2026).

borderRequirements.title: Passport & Entry Requirements
borderRequirements.schengenTitle: Romania is in the Schengen Area
borderRequirements.schengenDesc: Romania joined the European Schengen Zone for air and maritime borders in 2024 and full land borders. Passport control operates under unified Schengen regulations.
borderRequirements.passportValidity: Passport Validity: Your US/Canadian passport must remain valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure date from the Schengen territory (6 months validity is highly recommended).
borderRequirements.eesDesc: US and non-EU passport holders will undergo digital biometric registration (fingerprints and facial image) upon entry into Schengen ports. Monitor whether ETIAS electronic travel authorization is required for 2027 travel.

ground.title: Ground Transit: OTP to Bușteni
ground.subtitle: Bușteni is located approximately 120 km (75 miles) north of Bucharest OTP Airport along the scenic DN1 corridor through the Prahova Valley.
ground.driveTime: Typical transit time is 2 to 2.5 hours depending on weekend mountain traffic.

modes.title: Private Chauffeur / Shuttle Van
modes.pros: Door-to-door directly to your hotel; luggage handled; zero navigation stress after long flights.
modes.cons: Requires pre-booking with arrival flight details.
modes.services: Recommended operators: Daytrip (mydaytrip.com), Welcome Pickups, or City Airport Taxis.

modes.title: Direct Train (CFR & Astra Trans)
modes.pros: Bypasses all weekend highway traffic on DN1; beautiful mountain views approaching Bușteni.
modes.cons: Requires a 20-minute airport train to Bucharest Gara de Nord station before boarding the mountain train.
modes.services: CFR Călători or Astra Trans Carpatic (comfortable private carrier with clean assigned seating).

modes.title: Rental Car at OTP Airport
modes.pros: Complete independence to explore Bran Castle, Brașov, and alpine viewpoints.
modes.cons: Heavier weekend traffic on DN1; Romanian road rules require 0.0 alcohol tolerance.
modes.services: Important: Book AUTOMATIC transmission early (manual is default in Europe); carry International Driving Permit (IDP); verify rovinietă (road vignette).

lodging.subtitle: Selected hubs across the Prahova Valley and Southern Transylvania

roomBlock.desc: We are currently finalizing group room blocks with preferred rates across Bușteni and Sinaia. Details and booking discount codes will be released here by late 2026. Please reserve by February 2027.

hubs.name: Bușteni (Venue Town)
hubs.vibe: Alpine serenity, walking distance to castle and cable car
hubs.desc: Perfect if you want to be within steps or a 3-minute cab of all wedding celebrations. Numerous charming boutique pensiuni (Romanian mountain chalets and villas) with wooden balconies and mountain views.
hubs.picks: Villa Leonida, Pensiunea Silva, Pensiunea Cantacuzino, boutique villas on Strada Zamora.

hubs.name: Sinaia (Royal Spa Town)
hubs.vibe: Historic Belle Époque architecture, royal parklands, Peleș Castle
hubs.desc: The summer residence of Romanian royalty. Full of historic 4-star and 5-star spa hotels, lively pedestrian promenades, outdoor cafes, and excellent restaurants.
hubs.picks: Hotel International Sinaia, Alexandrion Experience / New Montana, Hotel Rina Sinaia, Villa Obelisc.

hubs.name: Brașov (Medieval Saxon City)
hubs.vibe: Vibrant medieval cobblestone streets, Gothic Black Church, boutique nightlife
hubs.desc: Transylvania's crown jewel. Ideal for guests who want to stay in a bustling historical city with sprawling cafes around Piața Sfatului (Council Square) and take wedding shuttles south into Bușteni.
hubs.picks: Radisson Blu Aurum Brașov, Aro Palace, Hotel Casa Chitic, Schuster Boarding House.

lore.title: Regional Lore & Travel Itineraries
lore.subtitle: Curated deep dives into the history, legends, and extended journeys across Romania
lore.cantacuzinoTitle: Castelul Cantacuzino: The Prince's Alpine Vision
lore.cantacuzinoExcerpt: Completed in 1911 by Prince Gheorghe Grigore Cantacuzino ('Nababul' — The Nabob), one of the wealthiest landowners and Prime Ministers of Romania.
lore.cantacuzinoFull: Perched on the Zamora plateau overlooking the Bușteni valley, Castelul Cantacuzino was designed by architect Grigore Cerchez in the distinctive Neo-Romanian (Brâncovenesc) style. The castle features hand-carved oak ceilings, Carrera marble stairs, Venetian stained glass, and a unique heraldic gallery displaying the blazons of the Cantacuzino dynasty. In recent years, its striking Gothic-Romanesque silhouette gained international fame as the filming location for 'Nevermore Academy' in Netflix's global hit Wednesday.
lore.pelesTitle: Castelul Peleș: A Royal Masterpiece in Sinaia
lore.pelesExcerpt: Commissioned in 1873 by King Carol I of Romania, Peleș was hailed as one of the most technologically advanced and architecturally breathtaking palaces in Europe.
lore.pelesFull: Surrounded by pine forests in Sinaia, Peleș Castle was the first castle in Europe to have central heating, an electric elevator, and its own hydro-electric power plant. Its 160 rooms display extraordinary German Renaissance woodwork, Murano crystal chandeliers, hand-painted Swiss glass, and an immense armory containing over 4,000 European and Oriental weapons.
lore.transylvaniaExcerpt: An unforgettable driving or private tour through medieval Saxon fortified churches, UNESCO heritage citadels, and storybook villages.
lore.transylvaniaFull:
Recommended route:
• Day 1-3: Bușteni, Sinaia (Peleș), and the dramatic towers of Bran Castle.
• Day 4: Medieval Brașov & the UNESCO fortified church village of Viscri (where King Charles III preserves historic Saxon heritage homes).
• Day 5: Sighișoara — the only continuously inhabited medieval citadel in Eastern Europe and birthplace of Vlad III Țepeș (The Impaler).
• Day 6-7: Sibiu — European Capital of Culture, famous for its 'houses with eyes', Bridge of Lies, and vibrant culinary scene.
lore.deltaExcerpt: For adventurous travelers: explore Europe's largest pristine wetland sanctuary followed by the historic Black Sea coast.
lore.deltaFull: From Bucharest or Transylvania, travel east to Tulcea, the gateway to the UNESCO Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve. Board private wooden skiffs to weave through secluded water channels filled with white water lilies, migrating European pelicans, and wild horses in the Letea Forest. Finish your journey in Constanța, viewing the iconic Art Nouveau Casino on the Black Sea promenade.

tips.title: Essential Practical Information
tips.subtitle: Helpful insights for smooth travel throughout Romania

items.title: Currency & Payments
items.desc: The national currency is the Romanian Leu (RON). Credit cards and contactless Apple Pay / Google Pay are accepted virtually everywhere (restaurants, taxis, shops). Keep a small amount of cash (100–200 RON) for small mountain souvenir stands or rural tipping.

items.title: Zero-Tolerance Driving
items.desc: Romania strictly enforces a 0.0‰ Blood Alcohol Concentration limit for all drivers — absolute zero tolerance. If you plan to enjoy Romanian wine or pălincă, always use our wedding shuttles or local taxis. Always use Waze for navigation on DN1 to track police alerts and traffic.

items.title: Tipping Etiquette
items.desc: Tipping is customary in Romania. In restaurants and cafes, 10% is standard for good service (12–15% for exceptional service). Many restaurant card terminals now offer a tipping percentage prompt on screen.

items.title: Mountain & Wildlife Awareness
items.desc: The Carpathian Mountains are home to Europe's largest population of brown bears. While castle grounds and town centers are completely safe and monitored, never hike alone into unlit forests at dusk, never feed wildlife, and secure food waste.

items.title: Connectivity & SIMs
items.desc: Romania possesses some of the fastest broadband and 5G mobile networks in the world. US travelers can enable an international roaming plan or install an inexpensive local eSIM (Airalo, Maya Mobile, or Orange Romania) in seconds.

items.title: Electrical Plugs & Voltage
items.desc: Standard European electrical plugs (Type C & F, 230V / 50Hz). North American travelers will need plug adapters for phones and laptops, and dual-voltage appliances for heated hair tools.
